name: CC6 Logical and Physical Access Controls Relationship Set
description: Authoritative relationship graph for the CC6 vertical slice. Extends, and does not replace, MAPSET-ACCESS-CORE: edges already declared there are not repeated here. The relationship vocabulary is identical across both sets and the validator enforces that identically-named relationship types carry identical definitions.

traversal_notes: Edges are derived from the entity records themselves, so the convenience references on controls, evidence, questions, findings, and remediations and the authoritative graph cannot diverge. The validator checks the agreement in both directions.

Every relationship is traversable in reverse via its declared inverse; 'which evidence supports this control' and 'which controls does this evidence support' are the same edge read from opposite ends.
finding_affects_criterion exists so a gap can be reported against a criterion even where the entity has articulated no control at all.
Policy-to-criterion and evidence-to-criterion relationships remain derived by traversal through controls rather than stored, so there is no second source of truth to drift.

relationship_types.answers_question: Which evidence supports this control, and which controls does this evidence support?

mappings.rationale: Multi-Factor Authentication for Access to In-Scope Systems contributes to CC6.7 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.1; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.1: Reduce the value of physical or storage-layer access to protected information by rendering stored data unreadable without a key, and keep the keys themselves under controlled, attributable custody.

Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management contributes to CC6.5 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.1; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management contributes to CC6.7 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.1; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.
Encryption at Rest and Key Management Configuration is primary evidence for Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management: Encryption settings and key policy across in-scope storage.
Configuration Change History and Drift Record is supporting evidence for Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management: Converts point-in-time encryption state into period coverage.
Cryptography and Key Management Policy is where the standard Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management is measured against originates.
Data Classification and Handling Policy is where the standard Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management is measured against originates.

Assesses Encryption of Data at Rest and Cryptographic Key Management. Question intent: Establish encryption coverage including backups, and whether key custody is separated from data access, which determines what the control actually mitigates.

Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.2: Ensure that credentials are issued only to identities that have been verified and whose access has been authorised by someone with the standing to grant it, before access is granted rather than after.

Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users contributes to CC6.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.2; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users contributes to CC6.3 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.2; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Access Provisioning Authorization Record is primary evidence for Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users: The approval record itself, joined to the account creation event.

Multi-Factor Authentication Enforcement Configuration is supporting evidence for Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users: Identity provider export establishes the account population to reconcile approvals against.
Access Control Policy is where the standard Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users is measured against originates.

Assesses Authorized Registration and Provisioning of Internal and External Users. Question intent: Establish whether authorisation precedes provisioning and whether it names the entitlement, which is what makes an approval evidential rather than ceremonial.

Timely Removal of Access on Termination and Role Change is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.2: Ensure credentials and entitlements cease to be usable once the authorisation basis for them ends, within a timeframe the entity has committed to and can measure.

Timely Removal of Access on Termination and Role Change contributes to CC6.3 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.2; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.
User Access Review Record is primary evidence for Timely Removal of Access on Termination and Role Change: Entitlement state and revocation records reconciled to the termination population.
Multi-Factor Authentication Enforcement Configuration is supporting evidence for Timely Removal of Access on Termination and Role Change: Identity provider account state corroborating revocation.
Access Control Policy is where the standard Timely Removal of Access on Termination and Role Change is measured against originates.
Assesses Timely Removal of Access on Termination and Role Change. Question intent: Establish the self-defined commitment and whether adherence to it is measurable at all.
Periodic User Access Review contributes to CC6.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.3; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.3: Ensure entitlements are granted against defined roles rather than ad hoc, that privilege is no broader than the role requires, and that administrative capability is held temporarily and attributably rather than standing.

Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management contributes to CC6.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.3; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management contributes to CC6.2 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.3; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Privileged Access Inventory and Elevation Record is primary evidence for Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management: Privileged entitlement inventory and elevation records across the period.
User Access Review Record is supporting evidence for Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management: Review record corroborates role assignment appropriateness.
Access Provisioning Authorization Record is supporting evidence for Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management: Approvals show whether grants referenced defined roles.
Access Control Policy is where the standard Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management is measured against originates.

Assesses Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management. Question intent: Distinguish standing privilege from just-in-time elevation, which is the single largest differentiator in CC6.3 risk.
Assesses Role-Based Least Privilege and Privileged Access Management. Question intent: Surface attribution gaps, which undermine every access control that depends on knowing who did something.

Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.4: Restrict physical entry to facilities and locations holding protected information assets to people whose role requires it, and be able to show who held that access and why throughout the period.

Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets contributes to CC6.5 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.4; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Physical Access Roster and Review Record is primary evidence for Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets: Access roster and the periodic review of it, with revocation records.

Subservice Organization Assurance Report is primary evidence for Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets: Where facilities are hosted, the subservice organization's assurance report is the primary evidence.
Physical Security Policy is where the standard Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets is measured against originates.

Assesses Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets. Question intent: Establish whether CC6.4 is met through the entity's own controls, through subservice organization reliance, or both. This determines what evidence is even relevant.

Assesses Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets. Question intent: Detect the split-lifecycle pattern, where logical deprovisioning is automated and physical revocation is a separate manual step that is forgotten.

Assesses Physical Access Restriction to Facilities and Protected Information Assets. Question intent: Establish that the review occurs on cadence and produces correction, rather than existing as an inventory exercise.

Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.5: Ensure that protections are not withdrawn from an asset until the data on it can no longer be read or recovered, so that end-of-life equipment and media do not become an uncontrolled disclosure path.
Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization contributes to CC6.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.5; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.
Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization contributes to CC6.4 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.5; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Encryption at Rest and Key Management Configuration is supporting evidence for Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization: Where cryptographic erasure is relied on, key custody and destruction evidence is required.
Asset Management and Media Sanitization Policy is where the standard Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization is measured against originates.
Data Classification and Handling Policy is where the standard Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization is measured against originates.

Assesses Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization. Question intent: Establish whether sanitization is evidenced per asset and whether all departure routes are covered, not only destruction at end of life.
Assesses Secure Decommissioning and Media Sanitization. Question intent: Test the cloud-equivalent path for CC6.5, which is frequently assumed to need no evidence at all.

External Boundary Protection is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.6: Reduce exposure of in-scope systems to threats originating outside the system boundary by constraining what can be reached from outside, protecting credentials crossing the boundary, and detecting attempts against external access points.
External Boundary Protection contributes to CC6.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.6; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.
External Boundary Protection contributes to CC6.7 in addition to its primary criterion CC6.6; DriftGuard models the overlap as a secondary edge rather than duplicating the control.

Configuration Change History and Drift Record is primary evidence for External Boundary Protection: Change history and drift detection converting point-in-time state into period coverage.
Multi-Factor Authentication Enforcement Configuration is supporting evidence for External Boundary Protection: Additional authentication for access from outside the boundary.
Network and Boundary Security Policy is where the standard External Boundary Protection is measured against originates.
Assesses External Boundary Protection. Question intent: Surface the highest-impact boundary exposure, and separate intended exposure from accidental exposure, which look identical in a rule export.

Assesses External Boundary Protection. Question intent: Establish whether drift is detected continuously or discovered at review time, which determines whether the control can evidence a period at all.
Assesses External Boundary Protection. Question intent: Test for the most common drift mechanism: a temporary rule with no expiry and no owner.

Protection of Information During Transmission, Movement, and Removal is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.7: Restrict who and what may move protected information out of the environment, and keep that information protected while it is in motion or on portable media.

Assesses Protection of Information During Transmission, Movement, and Removal. Question intent: Separate configured intent from deployed behaviour, and establish whether verification covers API and integration endpoints or only the public web endpoint.

Prevention and Detection of Unauthorized and Malicious Software is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC6.8: Prevent unauthorised or malicious software from being introduced into the environment where practical, detect it where prevention is not, and act on what is detected.

notes: Edge rationales are composed from the source entity records rather than written independently, which is deliberate: a hand-written rationale that drifts from the record it describes is worse than none. The substantive judgement lives in the entity record and is cited here.
MAP identifiers continue the single sequence begun in MAPSET-ACCESS-CORE. Identifiers are permanent and are never renumbered when edges are added.
Cross-framework mappings to NIST, ISO, and CIS remain attributes of the control records rather than edges here.

MAP-0231 to MAP-0233 added after the validator's bidirectional evidence check identified three evidence records asserting applicability to controls that did not reciprocate. The controls were corrected rather than the evidence, since the relationships were legitimate.
